item.title: Court ​‌‍‍‍‍⁠⁠‍​⁠⁠​​​​‍‌​dismisses Sowore’s request seeking DSS DG to testify in his defence
item.description: The Federal High Court in Abuja on Monday dismissed an application by Omoyele Sowore, publisher of Sahara Reporters, seeking an order compelling the Director-General (DG) of Department of State Services (DSS), Mr Oluwatosin Ajayi, to testify in his defence. Justice Mohammed Umar, in a ruling, held that the application by Sowore, the presidential candidate of Action Action Congress (AAC), would not serve the interest of justice. Justice Umar held that the DG or any designated officer of the service who had full knowledge of its official and other relevant business could testify before this court for the defendant (Sowore). The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that Sowore is being prosecuted by the DSS on allegations bordering on cybercrime. The defendant was alleged to have, in August 2025, published posts on X (formerly Twitter) and Facebook, describing President Bola Tinubu as a “criminal” and accusing him of lying about the level of corruption in the country. Sowore, through his lawyer, Adeyinka Olumide Fusika, SAN, had sought an order of the court compelling the DG’s appearance to testify relating to the cyberbullying case instituted against him. The DSS’ lawyer, Akinlolu Kehinde, SAN, had opposed the move, arguing that another official of the agency could testify on his behalf. The senior lawyer argued that it was absurd for Sowore to insist on the DSS DG’s appearance in court in an action that was purely official and not personal. In his ruling, Justice Umar agreed with Kehinde’s argument that the subpoena concerned an official act of the DSS and that the expected testimony was not personal to the DG. According to the judge the testimony that is expected from the Director General is not personal, but in respect of an official act or engagement. Justice Umar consequently ruled that another DSS official could appear to give evidence on the agency’s behalf. Following the ruling, defence counsel called the 3rd defence witness, Michael Jego, an investigating officer with the DSS. Jego said he was a member of the DSS investigation team which flagged the controversial post of Sowore on X and Facebook and subsequently advised him to retract it. ‎ ‎The witness said the posts made on 26 Aug. 2025 had the potential of posing a significant threat to national security. The witness told the court that he was part of an investigation team that monitored reactions with relation to the post. item.title: ‘Tell Them No’ – Obi urges UK-based Nigerians to stop sending money home
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye The presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, has urged Nigerians living in the United Kingdom to stop giving money to people in Nigeria who ask them for financial help, saying continued assistance may ease the effects of hardship without addressing its underlying causes. Obi attributed Nigeria’s economic hardship to poor leadership and argued that financial assistance does not address that problem, urging Nigerians in the diaspora to encourage their relatives and friends at home to vote for productive leaders. “You have people at home in Nigeria today who are begging you for money. Tell them no!” Obi said at a town hall meeting with diaspora supporters in Manchester on Sunday. He argued that people’s continued need for financial help was connected to the country’s economic difficulties, which he blamed on poor governance. In his view, sending money can cushion the hardship people face, but it does not resolve the problems that have left them seeking assistance. The former Anambra State governor also pointed to his record in public office, saying he had saved public funds during his tenure. He acknowledged that he was not perfect but argued that his record set him apart from other governors. “I’m not saying I’m a saint, but I saved money. I’ve not seen one governor who has saved 10 per cent of what I saved. No governor has done it,” Obi said. He further challenged other governors to match the savings he said he achieved while in office, saying, “I was not the only governor, and I challenge people if one governor can save 10 per cent of the money I saved, but there is nobody that did that.” The NDC presidential candidate further implored Nigerians to begin by supporting leaders they consider less corrupt. “Let’s start with this one that is less corrupt. That’s how other countries change,” he added. He also said his conversations with people reinforced the need for collective responsibility, adding that building a new Nigeria would require citizens to take an active role in addressing the country’s challenges. Obi urged Nigerians to take the 2027 election seriously, describing it as a critical moment for the country. item.title: Japan to launch world-first mission to moon of Mars
item.description: Japanese scientists will launch a spacecraft on Tuesday that aims to be the first to retrieve samples from one of Mars’s moons, potentially helping unlock the origins of the Solar System and life on Earth. The flagship H3 rocket carrying the unmanned Martian Moons eXploration (MMX) probe is set to blast off from the Tanegashima Space Center at 4:41 am (1941 GMT Monday), according to the Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA). If successful, the spacecraft will arrive near Mars around August next year, where it will orbit one of its moons, Phobos. It will later land on Phobos and collect at least 10 grams (0.35 ounces) of material from the surface during its planned three years in the Red Planet’s vicinity. The mission — which aims to be the first round trip to the Martian region — is a collaboration with US and European space agencies, as well as numerous universities and tech companies. Those involved hope that it will help lay the groundwork for eventual human exploration. JAXA hopes the mission will reveal how Mars and its two moons formed, a key piece of knowledge in working out how the Solar System was born. One theory for the origin of the moons — the “giant impact” hypothesis — is that they formed after a celestial body collided with Mars. The “capture” hypothesis, meanwhile, postulates that the moons are asteroids pulled in by Mars’s gravity. Determining which theory is correct will help reveal “how a habitable environment for life might have arisen on the terrestrial planets”, JAXA said, referring to the four rocky worlds closest to the Sun — Mercury, Venus, Earth and Mars. – ‘Natural space station’ – JAXA said the mission will also explore the possibility of using Phobos as a “natural space station” by establishing the requirements for a round trip — something “essential for crewed Mars exploration”. It will also observe the planet’s other moon, Deimos, although it will not land on it. US and Chinese space agencies have also been vying to be the first to return rock samples from Mars’s surface back to Earth. NASA’s Perseverance rover, which has been roaming across Mars since 2021, has already collected samples. The return mission, however, was effectively cancelled by the administration of President Donald Trump following a vote by Congress in January. China’s Tianwen-3 spacecraft is scheduled for launch around 2028 and hopes to return Mars samples to Earth as early as 2031 — potentially before the Japanese mission’s return. item.title: CAN mourns Uduaghan, hails commitment to national unity
item.description: By Luminous Jannamike The Christian Association of Nigeria (CAN) has mourned former Delta State Governor, Dr Emmanuel Eweta Uduaghan, praising his commitment to dialogue and confidence-building during a period of heightened political tension in Nigeria. The association said Uduaghan’s efforts to promote understanding and preserve national unity remained an important part of his contributions to public service and nation-building. In a statement on Monday, CAN President, Archbishop Daniel Okoh, expressed sadness over the former governor’s death and extended the association’s sympathies to his family, the Delta State Government and the people of Delta State, as well as all those mourning him. “His commitment to dialogue, confidence-building and the preservation of national unity remains worthy of commendation,” Archbishop Okoh said. He described Uduaghan’s passing as a loss to his family and all who valued his contributions to public service and nation-building. Archbishop Okoh prayed for God’s comfort for the bereaved family and others affected by the loss, asking God to grant the former governor eternal rest. item.title: Man City’s Guehi questions impact of taking the knee in fight against racism
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Manchester City defender Marc Guehi believes taking the knee before football matches may have lost some of its impact saying more can be done to tackle racism. According to the Associated Press, Guehi, who is Black, did not take the knee before City’s Premier League match against Ipswich on Saturday, the first of two rounds of games dedicated to the league’s “No Room For Racism” campaign. It isn’t the first time Guehi refused to perform the gesture. The gesture was introduced in June 2020 in support of the Black Lives Matter movement. The Premier League stopped asking players to take the knee before every match from the 2022-23 season, instead inviting them to do so on selected occasions. Speaking on Monday, ahead of City’s Champions League match against AEK Athens, Guehi welcomed the continuation of the anti-racism campaign and called for further action. “It’s great,” he said. “Whether more can be done — more can always be done. We have to see how we can move the campaign along. “I don’t think it’s necessarily a football issue. I think it’s a wider societal issue and football is that beacon of hope to try to get the message out. But whether more can be done, we will try, hopefully with the PFA (English soccer’s players union), with the league.” Asked whether taking the knee had lost its meaning, Guehi replied: “Maybe. I haven’t been taking the knee for a while now, to be honest. I’d always clap, just because of what that actually signifies.” He did not elaborate on his reasons for no longer taking the knee. Leeds striker Dominic Calvert-Lewin also remained standing during the weekend’s anti-racism gesture, while his teammates and Manchester United players knelt. Calvert-Lewin scored in the 1-1 draw. Leeds manager Daniel Farke said: “Dom is more or less like, ‘No, I don’t go down. I show my respect by standing up, more or less.’ “I think each individual is different and shows respect for this campaign in a different way.” Former Crystal Palace forward Wilfried Zaha, who is Black, said in 2021 that he would no longer take the knee, describing the gesture as “degrading”. “I feel like taking a knee is degrading,” Zaha was quoted by The Guardian as telling the FT Business of Football conference. “Growing up, my parents just let me know that I should just be proud to be black, no matter what, and I just think we should stand tall. “I think the meaning behind the whole thing is becoming something that we just do now. That’s not enough.” The Premier League’s “No Room For Racism” initiative takes place during the UK’s Black History Month. League chief executive Richard Masters said it aims to use “the reach of our players to send an important message: we are united in the fight against racism.” The post Man City’s Guehi questions impact of taking the knee in fight against racism appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Rivers assembly set to recall three suspended Pro-Fubara lawmakers
item.description: By Davies Iheamnachor, Port Harcourt The Rivers State House of Assembly has reversed its earlier decision to declare the seats of three lawmakers supporting the state governor, Siminalayi Fubara, vacant. The state’s legislative arm reached this resolution to reinstate the three lawmakers during its plenary on Monday. The pro-Fubara lawmakers, whose seats were earlier marked to be declared vacant, included Hon. Victor Oko-Jumbo, representing Bonny Constituency. Hon. Sokari Goodboy Sokari, Ahoada West and Hon. Orubienimigha Timothy, Opobo/Nkoro Constituency. The assembly decision followed letters dated 16th of October 2026 from the three lawmakers, which were read on the floor of the House during plenary. The lawmakers in the letter requested that they be called back into the House to continue the representation of the constituency with the emergence of peace. It would be recalled that the House of Assembly had, on the 30th October 2023, in the heat of the political crisis, suspended the three lawmakers alongside Hon. Edison Ehie for alleged misconduct. Ehie, who later became the Chief of Staff to the Governor, had resigned his membership of the assembly in the heat of the crisis, allowing for a by-election in his constituency. The trio’s suspension was, however, lifted on the 20th of December 2023 after the first peace meeting initiated by President Tinubu between the Minister of the Federal Capital Territory, Nyesom Wike and Governor Fubara. But following the failure of the three lawmakers to attend sittings after their suspension was lifted, their seats were then declared vacant on the 15th of October 2025 by the Amaewhule-led House in line with section 109 sub 1 (e) of the Constitution. The House had consequently written the Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC, to conduct a by-election to fill the vacant seats. But during Monday’s plenary, the Speaker, Rt. Hon. Martin Amaewhule read the letters from each of the three lawmakers explaining that they never saw the letter lifting their suspension earlier, which was the reason they didn’t attend the sitting and appealed for the House to rescind its decision. After debates on the letter by the lawmakers, the House decided to rescind its decision to declare their seats vacant The assembly’s decision might not be unconnected with Sunday’s meeting between the Leader of Rainbow Coalition and Minister of the Federal Capital Territory, Chief Nyesom Wike, the lawmakers, Chairmen of Local Government Areas and other leaders of the coalition with the Governor, Fubara and members of his team. It was gathered that the letters that preceded and the decision of the Assembly were issues resolved at the strategic closed-door meeting. It was further gathered the meeting which had Senator Magnus Abe was aimed at resolving outstanding areas of differences between the two political camps of Wike and Fubara ahead of the 2027 general elections. item.title: Makinde campaign knocks Tinubu over poverty, N166.7trn debt
item.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA – The Makinde-Daura Presidential Campaign Organisation (MDPCO) has accused President Bola Tinubu’s administration of pushing Nigeria towards collapse, citing widespread poverty, mounting public debt and worsening insecurity. The organisation said the country’s economic hardship and declining public confidence demanded a change of direction, urging Nigerians to consider Oyo State Governor Seyi Makinde’s proposed RESET NIGERIA agenda. In a statement by its Director of Strategic Communications, Richard Nnanna Ihediwa, on Monday, the campaign organisation cited a World Bank estimate that about 140 million Nigerians were living in poverty, accusing the All Progressives Congress (APC) administration of failing to ease citizens’ hardship. It also faulted the Federal Government’s borrowing strategy, citing public debt of about N166.7 trillion and plans to secure another $1.5 billion in World Bank financing. “President Tinubu is burying Nigeria by instalment, saddling the nation with a debt burden her future generation won’t be able to pay,” the organisation said. The MDPCO warned that continued borrowing without a clear repayment strategy could deepen the country’s economic difficulties, arguing that mounting debt had yet to translate into meaningful improvements in citizens’ lives. It also cited poor educational outcomes and Nigeria’s infrastructure deficit as evidence of the country’s development challenges, while accusing the administration of weakening public confidence through its handling of the economy and security. Describing the 2027 presidential election as an opportunity to change the country’s direction, the organisation said Makinde’s RESET NIGERIA agenda would prioritise economic growth, transparency, social stability and reforms in education, security and productive sectors. The campaign organisation urged Nigerians to use their votes to demand accountability and determine the country’s political future. item.title: Inflation: Jigawa to increase NYSC members’ allowance — Namadi
item.description: By Muhammad Inuwa, Dutse The Jigawa State Government has announced plans to increase the ₦5,000 monthly allowance paid to National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) members serving in the state to cushion the effects of rising inflation. Governor Umar Namadi disclosed this while addressing Batch C corps members at the Yakubu Gowon NYSC Orientation Camp in Fanisau, Dutse. Namadi acknowledged the contributions of corps members to community development, saying the government would review their allowance to improve their welfare amid rising living costs. “We are aware of your contributions in our communities. Therefore, we will look into and review your monthly allowance to help you manage the effects of recent inflation,” he said. He commended President Bola Tinubu’s administration for increasing the federal monthly allowance for corps members to ₦77,000, assuring them that Jigawa would also review its payment. “On our part, we will follow the footsteps of the Federal Government to review and increase your monthly state allowance,” he added. The governor also announced a one-off settlement allowance of ₦10,000 for each corps member at the end of the three-week orientation programme to assist them in moving to their primary places of assignment. “We will also give each of you ₦10,000 so that when you are posted to your various primary places of assignment, you will have something in your pocket,” he said. Namadi urged ministries, departments and agencies to make adequate arrangements to receive corps members posted to their offices and ensure a smooth transition from the orientation camp to their places of primary assignment. He further pledged to renovate the orientation camp, construct a new hall and provide a standby generator to improve facilities and ensure a reliable power supply. Describing Jigawa as a peaceful state with hospitable residents, the governor encouraged corps members to integrate into their host communities and contribute meaningfully to local development. He congratulated them on their deployment to the state and wished them a successful service year. item.title: Things to know about late ex-Delta gov Uduaghan
item.description: Former Governor of Delta State, Dr. Emmanuel Uduaghan, is dead. Uduaghan passed away on the morning of Monday, according to a press statement by Toju Uduaghan, on behalf of the family. It partly read, “It is with hearts weighed down by immeasurable grief and profound sorrow that we announce the passing to glory of our beloved Father, Brother, Uncle, and Patriarch, His Excellency, Dr. Chief Emmanuel Eweta Uduaghan, former Governor of Delta State, who departed this world on the morning of 19th October 2026. “His passing has left us devastated. Words can hardly express the depth of our sorrow at the loss of a man who meant so much to our family and whose life and service touched countless others across Delta State and Nigeria.” Things to know about late Uduaghan He was born on 22 October 1954 in Warri North Local Government Area of Delta State. He attended Baptist Primary School, Mosogar, between 1961 and 1966; Federal Government College, Warri, between 1968 and 1974; and the University of Benin between 1975 and 1980, earning a Bachelor of Medicine and Surgery (MBBS) degree and a Diploma in Anaesthesia. He was posted to Kwara State for the mandatory one-year National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) in 1981. Between 1989 and 1994, late Uduaghan served in a number of healthcare facilities, such as Shell Clinic Ogunu, Westend Hospital Warri and Benoni Clinic Benin City, Edo State. On return to democracy in 1999, he was appointed as commissioner for health in Delta state. In 2003, Uduaghan was appointed Secretary to the Delta State Government. In 2007, he was elected as governor of Delta State and subsequently re-elected in 2011. On 29 August 2018, he officially announced he had left PDP for APC and returned to the party in 2020. item.title: FG Reaffirms Commitment To Human Capital Development For Economic Growth
item.description: The Federal Government has reaffirmed its commitment to human capital development as a central pillar for economic growth, saying long-term investments in health, education, skills and livelihoods are critical to transforming Nigeria’s economy. The reaffirmation was made during a media engagement in Abuja on Monday organised to keep journalists abreast of developments under the Human Capital Development Programme (HCD) 2.0 and deepen public understanding of its role in national development. National Coordinator of the Human Capital Development 2.0 Programme, Rukayya El-Rufai, said Nigeria’s economic future depends on deliberate and sustained investment in its people. “Nigeria’s future depends on its people. If we do not invest in them, we cannot grow our economy. There’s a lot of investment going into infrastructure, but if you do not invest in human capital, you are not simply going to be able to grow your economy as much,” he said. item.title: Alleged Rights Violation: Court dismisses El-Rufai’s N120m suit
item.description: By Ikechukwu Nnochiri, Abuja A High Court of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT) sitting at Maitama, Abuja, on Monday dismissed a fundamental rights enforcement suit brought before it by the detained former governor of Kaduna State, Nasir El-Rufai. Listed as respondents in the legal action were the Department of State Services (DSS), the Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission (ICPC), the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC), and the Attorney General of the Federation (AGF). El-Rufai, who served as governor from 2015 to 2023 and as minister of the FCT under former President Olusegun Obasanjo’s administration, had accused the respondents in the suit of violating his rights. He further urged the court to invalidate letters of invitation extended to him by both the ICPC and the EFCC and demanded N120 million in damages from the respondents. Delivering judgment in the matter, Justice Sylvanus Oriji held that the legal action was without merit and dismissed it. The court held that the letters of invitation, which requested the former governor to appear before the federal agencies investigating allegations against him, met constitutional requirements and did not infringe his fundamental rights. The court held that the agencies acted within their mandates by inviting him to shed light on issues raised against him. Besides, the court declined to declare that the DSS’s attempt to arrest the applicant at Nnamdi Azikiwe Airport amounted to a violation of his rights. It held that the DSS has a statutory responsibility to maintain a watchlist and to arrest persons of interest. Justice Oriji held that the former governor could not use the court to stop government agencies from performing their legitimate duties. The court held that, contrary to El-Rufai’s contention, the agencies did not need a warrant to effect such an arrest. On whether the confiscation of the applicant’s international passport by the DSS was a violation of his rights, the court said it was satisfied that the seizure was lawful and carried out pursuant to the powers of the DSS. It held that the applicant failed to adduce evidence to establish that the seizure was continuous, permanent and unlawful. Consequently, aside from dismissing the case, the court awarded costs of N200,000 against the applicant in favour of each of the four respondents. item.title: CAS verdict on Senegal AFCON title appeal ‘expected end November’
item.description: The Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) announced Monday that a verdict on Senegal’s appeal of the decision to strip them of the Africa Cup of Nations title in favour of Morocco is expected at the end of November. CAS said in a statement that a hearing of the case took place behind closed doors at its headquarters in Lausanne on October 8. “The panel have begun and continue their deliberations,” the organisation which resolves international sports disputes explained. “The CAS arbitrators have decided to issue a complete ruling which includes legal grounds, known as a CAS Award. This process will require several weeks, with the CAS Award expected at the end of November 2026.” At the January 18 final in Rabat, Senegal won 1-0 thanks to Pape Gueye’s extra-time goal, but the occasion was marred by chaotic scenes near the end of normal time when many Senegal players walked off the pitch in protest at the decision to award Morocco a penalty with the match still goalless. Some Senegalese supporters also attempted a pitch invasion, and the game was held up for almost 20 minutes before the Senegal players returned. In March, the Confederation of African Football (CAF) overturned that result, awarding Morocco a 3-0 victory, and the title. item.title: Flood kills two, submerges 18 communities in Nasarawa
item.description: By Edwin Philip, Lafia The Nasarawa State Government has urged residents of flood-prone communities to heed evacuation warnings and move to higher ground following flooding that submerged 18 communities in the Doma Local Government Area, killing two people and displacing several others. The Commissioner for Information, Culture and Tourism, Dr Nawani Aboki, made the appeal on Monday while briefing journalists in Lafia on the impact of the disaster in the affected communities. Aboki said Governor Abdullahi Sule had directed the Director-General of the Nasarawa State Emergency Management Agency to visit the affected communities to assess the damage and determine the necessary interventions. He said the government was working towards providing assistance to residents affected by the disaster. “We are hoping that anytime this week concrete actions will be taken by government. Yesterday, when I was returning, I was there with the chairman of the local government to sympathise with the people and condole with them,” the commissioner said. According to him, two people have died as a result of the flooding, while several others have been displaced. Buildings and farmlands were also reportedly destroyed. Describing the incident as massive flooding, Aboki said residents had been advised against returning to their homes until the floodwaters receded. “It is not just normal flooding, but massive flooding that took place. We are hoping that the flooding will end and the waters dry up so that people can resume their normal activities,” he said. “But we have asked them not to go back yet. Let them wait until we see the water actually receding back to the River Benue. We are not sure if more water will be coming in from the Lagdo Dam in Cameroon; it will even be worse than it is currently,” he added. The commissioner said the government was also prepared to provide support and relief supplies to affected residents to reduce the risk of disease outbreaks following the flooding. He explained that several smaller communities were clustered within larger settlements, complicating efforts to assess the full extent of the damage and the number of people affected. Aboki cited Agyma, where more than eight communities were reportedly affected, and Rukubi and Akpanaja, where several communities were also said to be experiencing the impact of the flooding. The government urged residents in vulnerable areas to prioritise their safety and remain in safer locations until the floodwaters had sufficiently receded. The call came on Monday, October 19, 2026, as Nigeria marked the 40th anniversary of Giwa’s death. He was killed on October 19, 1986, by a parcel bomb delivered to his residence in Ikeja, Lagos. item.description: Ukraine did not receive an early warning from allies about incoming Russian ballistic strikes that targeted energy facilities in the Kyiv region, President Volodymyr Zelensky said on Monday. Russia launched 16 ballistic missiles at the Kyiv region and over 200 drones across the war-torn country, Zelensky said. AFP reporters heard air alerts and explosions ringing out in the capital. “Another Russian ballistic missile attack came in several waves overnight, and once again, there was no early warning from our partners,” Zelensky said on social media. Workers clear the rubble from a metro station following a Russian ballistic missile strike on Kyiv on October 19, 2026, amid the Russian invasion of Ukraine. Photo by SERGEI SUPINSKY / AFP Last week Kyiv said there had been no warning from the United States of similar strikes, leaving virtually no time for residents to take shelter. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio denied earlier on Monday that there had been any suspension of intelligence sharing with Ukraine. “There has been no pause,” Rubio told reporters in Uzbekistan when asked about Ukraine’s claims, calling on Zelensky to “focus” on ending the war with Russia. Trump, who says he has made a deal with Russia to secure fuel exports in exchange for the easing of sanctions, has made renewed attacks on Zelensky in recent days over the war. The US leader wrote on his Truth Social platform on Sunday that he was making “great progress” in negotiating peace between Russia and Ukraine, but claimed: “Zelenskyy doesn’t care, and frankly, with all of the money that Europe is famously giving him… he doesn’t want to end this war, and probably never did.” Workers clear the rubble from a metro station following a Russian ballistic missile strike on Kyiv on October 19, 2026, amid the Russian invasion of Ukraine. He said the council would convene a stakeholders’ meeting on Monday (today) to deliberate on the crisis and seek ways to prevent further violence. The chairman urged both warring parties to embrace peace and avoid actions capable of escalating tensions. He also called on youths in Paikon-Kore to exercise restraint and promote peaceful coexistence with other residents, warning against confrontation and retaliatory attacks. Ikwa advised farmers whose crops were damaged by cattle to report such incidents to the relevant security agencies rather than resorting to self-help. He noted that such conflicts often affected innocent people who might not even understand the circumstances that triggered the dispute. The chairman further urged residents to cooperate with security personnel deployed to the community, adding that an expanded security meeting had been convened, with youth leaders, the Sarkin Noma and other community leaders from both sides invited to seek a lasting solution. He said anyone who felt unfairly treated or believed their complaints had not received adequate attention should report directly to him for intervention, stressing that grievances must be addressed through lawful channels. Meanwhile, soldiers, police officers, vigilantes and personnel of the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC) have been deployed to the community to restore calm. The FCT Police Command spokesperson, SP Adeh Josephine, did not answer calls seeking the command’s reaction as of the time of filing this report. Not first clash Daily Trust recalls that the latest violence followed an earlier clash on August 11, 2026, across Paikon-Kore, Ibwa and Rafin-Zurfi communities, during which a farmer reportedly lost a hand and three other people sustained machete injuries. Following that incident, Ikwa summoned an emergency security meeting where traditional rulers, community leaders, village and district heads, Ardos of Fulanis, as well as representatives of various security agencies deliberated over the incessant farmers and herders clash. The chairman, at the end of the security meeting, set up a peace and investigative committee. He also carried out on-the-spot assessments of the three affected communities that witnessed cases of farmers and herders clashes. Ikwa promised that the committee’s report would be made public during the stakeholders meeting on Monday (today). Some residents, who spoke to our reporter, said the August 11 incident was a result of cows that allegedly strayed into a farm. They claimed that the tension heightened when the owner of the farm confronted the herders for allowing cows to graze inside his farm, a situation which they said led to a serious confrontation that left four persons injured. Ishaku Danjuma, a farmer, explained that a similar incident also happened in Paiko community on the same day, after some cows allegedly grazed inside a maize farm, resulting in clashes between farmers and herders in the community. He said the farmer queried the herders for allowing cows into the farm, which led to the clash. “If you make your investigations, you will discover that 95 per cent of incidents of farmers and herders clashes across the three communities were as a result of cows straying into people’s farms,” he said. A member of the Paiko community, Usman Yakubu, also said the incessant cases of farmers-herders clash were as a result of cows that allegedly invade farms to destroy crops in the rural communities in the area. He alleged that some herders allowed their cows to eat up some crops, a development he said led to serious confrontations between the affected farmers and the herders across the three communities. “It was as a result of the destruction of some crops which suddenly resulted in a confrontation between the affected farmers and herders, which later led to the injuring of four farmers across three villages,” he said. The reserve sits on 9,500 hectares of land but most of the area has also been encroached upon by the communities around the area according to herders.
